subject: Re: Post-demo latency & streaming triage — decision path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@orbitdata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: latency/streaming triage + proposed decision path

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo and a few clarifying items so we can lock the pilot configuration. I pulled the parts that matter for SLO qualification below.

Summary (what we showed)
- Live streaming demo with chunked token output, model variant: rdlw-13b-q4
- Continuous batching and KV caching enabled for repeated context
- Fallback path to cpu-quant variant for overflow

From the call, we heard your key requirements are latency for interactive flows, predictable throughput during peak sync jobs, and streaming fidelity for long responses. To make the pilot and acceptance criteria concrete, please confirm the items below:

Key asks (please confirm by EOD Tue)
1) Latency targets (p95): is your bar 250ms for interactive endpoints and 350ms acceptable for lower-priority streaming endpoints? (You mentioned ~300ms on the call — want to confirm exact numbers.)
2) Throughput: baseline steady traffic is ~150 RPS, but you said spikes up to ~500 concurrent streaming connections for a 10–15 minute window. Confirm typical test traffic profile and a target throughput we should validate.
3) Concurrency: do you consider 500 simultaneous streams as a hard SLO or a stress/burst requirement?
4) Streaming behavior: chunk size preferences, whether partial outputs are acceptable (you indicated yes), and whether you need token-by-token latency measured or just chunk-level latency.
5) Data: can you share a small representative trace (anonymized) and a short test prompt set (10–20 prompts) we can run against the pilot? See attached: demo-sample-trace.csv (sample trace columns + timestamps).

Proposed decision path / next steps (internal + external)
- Alex to confirm items 1–4 and share trace + procurement timeline (Laura CC'd) — target Tue EOD.
- Redwood to provision a 48-hour pilot environment (dedicated slot) with the streaming config and run the test prompt set.
- Measure p50/p95 token and chunk latencies, concurrency handling, and throughput with/without KV cache.
- If results meet decision criteria below, we convert pilot to a committed proof-of-use with reserved capacity.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft)
- Interactive endpoints: p95 <= 250ms for priority flows (90% of test set)
- Streaming endpoints: chunk-level p95 <= 350ms, end-to-end for long responses within expected tolerance
- No tail errors > 0.1% at target concurrency during a sustained 10-min window
- Fallback path succeeds within 500ms when capacity is exceeded

Please confirm and include any additional constraints (security/compliance evidence needs, IP allowlist, etc.). If you prefer, we can run a short smoke pilot first (4–6 hours) before the 48-hour run.

Thanks — attaching a small trace sample.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency/streaming triage + proposed decision path

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items below and adding detail from our side. Forwarding Laura to loop procurement.

On Thu, May 25, 2028 at 2:10 PM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo and a few clarifying items so we can lock the pilot configuration...

Answers from OrbitData:
- Latency targets: priority interactive endpoints — p95 target 300ms (we can stretch to 250ms if we see consistent results in pilot)
- Streaming endpoints: p95 chunk <= 350ms — end-to-end can be higher for very long responses
- Baseline throughput: ~150 RPS; spike profile: up to 500 concurrent streaming sessions for 10–20 minutes, with bursty arrival rate
- Concurrency: we treat 500 concurrent sessions as a hard burst target; our admin UX must stay responsive during spikes
- Streaming behavior: chunked outputs (clients assemble ordered chunks), prefer chunk sizes ~500–800 bytes; partial outputs are fine

Data and timeline:
- I'll share a sanitized trace and 15 prompts by EOD Monday.
- Procurement: Laura expects a 2–3 week procurement window once we agree on pilot terms.

Happy to run the smoke pilot first as you suggested. For the 48-hour pilot please include KV cache enabled and record both token-level latency and chunk-level latencies. Also flag any model fallback events in logs.

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform, OrbitData

Date: 2028-05-25T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: OrbitData pilot triage + MOP draft attached

Karthik / Tessa — forwarding Alex's confirmations. Key takeaways:
- OrbitData treats 500 concurrent streams as a hard burst target; baseline 150 RPS.
- Latency bar: 300ms p95 for priority interactive, 350ms chunk p95 for streaming (they can relax to 250ms if pilot results are strong).
- They will share a sanitized trace and 15 prompts by Mon EOD; procurement timeline ~2–3 weeks.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Tessa: prepare pilot MOP and config files (include KV cache on/off runs), propose pilot window and infra size — ETA Tue 9am PT. (Attachment: pilot-config-mop.docx)
- Karthik: confirm availability of AE/SE time to shadow pilot runs and review traces — propose two 2-hour slots next week.
- Ben: coordinate test harness and measurement dashboard; create HubSpot activity and update OD-4821 with pilot plan.

Decision criteria (draft) — we will use a three-tier pass/fail:
1) Pass: meets both interactive and streaming p95 targets for >90% of test prompts, <0.1% error tail at target concurrency.
2) Conditional: misses one latency target but shows consistent improvement with tuning; agree a remediation plan + follow-up run.
3) Fail: systemic tail latency or >0.5% errors at target concurrency with no clear mitigation in 48 hours.

I'll loop in CS if the pilot moves to committed. Please review the attached MOP and confirm owners.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

All — looks good. Tessa, please schedule the pilot slot for next Wednesday (UTC window 15:00–17:00 PT preferred) and reserve two SE hours the day after for root-cause analysis if we see regressions. Ben — I'll book the HubSpot activity and add OD-4821 notes.

Decision checklist (finalize before pilot)
- Confirm test prompt set + sanitized trace (Alex)
- Infra: two instance sizes (medium/high) to compare batching efficiency
- Telemetry: token-level, chunk-level, error rates, and fallback counts
- Acceptance owners: Karthik (technical), Ben (customer comms), Tessa (ops pilot run)

If we hit pass, we can move to a reserved capacity proposal. If conditional, we'll scope a remediation run (extra 24 hours) and then re-evaluate.

Thanks — Karthik
